name: mantyāsiḥ
source_citation: Atmodjo, Soekarto K. 1988, "Sekitar Masalah Hari Jadi Magelang" (paper; the quoted passages are in the first person and dated "makalah pertama [18 Juni 1988]"; no page numbers available)
url_or_file: https://sejarahjawaid.blogspot.com/2020/08/prasasti-poh.html (verbatim, unattributed repost of the Atmodjo text) ; https://budaya-indonesia.org/Asal-Usul-Magelang-1 (Kemendikbud portal, same identifications) ; https://magelangkotatua.wordpress.com/2010/02/06/prasasti-poh-dan-mantyasih/ (cites "Atmodjo, 1988") ; admin units: https://jateng.antaranews.com/berita/628505/prasasti-mantyasih-jejak-kota-magelang-1120-tahun
note: [read via: relay/reproduction; original NOT opened] [tier B] Epigrapher claim relayed by web pages. Atmodjo (UGM epigrapher who led the 1988 hari-jadi study) argues Mantyasih = Meteseh because Mantyasih I also names Mt Susundara/Sumwing, Wadung Poh, Kdu and Kuning Kagunturan, which he finds around Magelang. The identification is NOT from a findspot: the Mantyasih I plates came from the Ngadirejo/Parakan area (Temanggung). Kecamatan/kelurahan from ANTARA 2026 (Kampung Meteseh, Kel. Magelang, Kec. Magelang Tengah); Kel. Magelang 33.71.03.1004 exists in the E226 desa gazetteer. Context: the identification underpins the Magelang anniversary (Perda 6/1989), so treat with care. Applies to the Mantyasih of Mantyasih I/III (907); other mentions of Mantyasih as a witness village (Poh, Panggumulan A, Kayu Ara Hiwang, Rukam, Bhatari) are assumed, not shown, to be the same place.

name: mantyāsiḥ
modern_place: Matesih (west slope of Mt Lawu), Surakarta region
source_citation: Competing identification mentioned (and rejected) by Atmodjo 1988 ("bukan Matesih di Sala"); proposer not named in the text opened. DHARMA IDENK PROV_INS_01016 gives the findspot of the Mantyasih II stone as "? Matesih (lereng barat Gunung Lawu)".

name: vaduṁ poḥ
desa: Dumpoh (kampung/dusun) in Kelurahan Potrobangsan [admin units from the Novo Olshop blog, not from Atmodjo]
source_citation: Atmodjo, Soekarto K. 1988, "Sekitar Masalah Hari Jadi Magelang" (paper; the quoted passages are in the first person and dated "makalah pertama [18 Juni 1988]"; no page numbers available)
url_or_file: https://sejarahjawaid.blogspot.com/2020/08/prasasti-poh.html (verbatim, unattributed repost of the Atmodjo text) ; https://budaya-indonesia.org/Asal-Usul-Magelang-1 (Kemendikbud portal, same identifications) ; https://magelangkotatua.wordpress.com/2010/02/06/prasasti-poh-dan-mantyasih/ (cites "Atmodjo, 1988") ; http://novoolshop.blogspot.com/2018/03/prasasti-poh-batu-atau-emas.html (admin units)
note: [read via: relay/reproduction; original NOT opened] [tier B] Atmodjo: "wanua i wadung poh" -> Dung Poh -> Dumpoh [sebelah utara kota Magelang sekarang]. The same form vadum poh also appears in Wanua Tengah III and Taji Gunung (not shown to be the same place). Kel. Potrobangsan (33.71.02.1004, Kec. Magelang Utara) exists in the E226 gazetteer; Dumpoh itself is a sub-kelurahan name and is not in the desa-level gazetteer, so a centroid needs another source.

name: poḥ
source_citation: Magelang Kota Pusaka heritage group 2010 ("Prasasti Poh (905 M) terletak di Kampung Poh (sekarang Dumpoh)"); Novo Olshop blog 2018 ("desa Poh ... sering diidentikkan dengan desa Dumpoh"). No epigrapher is named for this equation.
note: [read via: read directly] [tier C] NOT an epigrapher/archaeologist source - include only if the PI accepts local-historian claims. Atmodjo identifies only "Wadung Poh" with Dumpoh, not "Poh". The Poh plates were found at Plembon, Randusari, Prambanan (Klaten). A DHARMA editor (Griffiths, commentary of DHARMA_INSIDENKHampran.xml) calls "the identifications on the modern map for epigraphic toponym Poh proposed by Kusen" not particularly convincing and notes that Poh (= mango) is a generic toponym used in more than one area. The frame key "poh" merges several referents (Poh, Poh Pitu, Rake Wanua Poh ...). RECOMMEND: treat key "poh" as I3 (ambiguous) and do not use it for matching.

name: kuniṁ
modern_place: Kembang Kuning and Guntur (the "Kuning Kagunturan" of Mantyasih I)
desa: Rejosari (source: "Kal. Rejosari"); Kembang Kuning and Guntur are sub-desa names given by the source
kabupaten: Magelang (kabupaten not stated by the source; Bandongan is a kecamatan of Kab. Magelang)
source_citation: Atmodjo, Soekarto K. 1988, "Sekitar Masalah Hari Jadi Magelang" (paper; the quoted passages are in the first person and dated "makalah pertama [18 Juni 1988]"; no page numbers available)
url_or_file: https://sejarahjawaid.blogspot.com/2020/08/prasasti-poh.html (verbatim, unattributed repost of the Atmodjo text) ; https://budaya-indonesia.org/Asal-Usul-Magelang-1 (Kemendikbud portal, same identifications) ; https://magelangkotatua.wordpress.com/2010/02/06/prasasti-poh-dan-mantyasih/ (cites "Atmodjo, 1988")
note: [read via: relay/reproduction; original NOT opened] [tier B] Atmodjo: "wanua ing kuning ... Kuning Kagunturan" = desa Kembang Kuning dan Guntur [Kal. Rejosari, Kec. Bandongan], NW of Meteseh; "tidak perlu dijelaskan lebih lanjut" (stated without hedge, on name survival + proximity to Mantyasih). Desa Rejosari exists in Kec. Bandongan (33.08.14.2014) in the E226 gazetteer; no desa Kembang Kuning exists in Bandongan, so these are dusun names. Applies to Mantyasih I/II/III.

source_citation: Atmodjo, Soekarto K. 1988, "Sekitar Masalah Hari Jadi Magelang" (paper; the quoted passages are in the first person and dated "makalah pertama [18 Juni 1988]"; no page numbers available)

note: [read via: relay/reproduction; original NOT opened] [tier B] Atmodjo: "Galang [Glam] dan Glangglang mungkin berubah menjadi Gelang atau Magelang sekarang [awalan ma-]" (hedged). Etymological claim about the name Magelang, no desa-level location; weak for matching. Poh names Glangglang and Galang; Gilikan I names "bhatara i Glam". name: hinapit
source_citation: Soekarto (initials and year not given by the relaying source), as relayed by Ahmad Yasin, Kompas.com 19 Jun 2025, "Asal-usul Nama Candi Prambanan dan Dua Versi Cerita Pembangunannya"
note: [read via: secondary only; primary NOT opened] [tier B] "Cepit (Hinapit)". Primary publication of the Soekarto claim not identified or opened. The systematic source is probably Kusen 1990/1991, "Identifikasi Toponim dalam Prasasti Jawa Kuno Abad IX-X dari Prambanan dan Sekitarnya dengan Toponim Masa Kini" (UGM research report; cited in the Indonesian Wikipedia article Prasasti Tulang Air I), NOT accessible. name: paṁramuan
source_citation: Soekarto (initials and year not given by the relaying source), as relayed by Ahmad Yasin, Kompas.com 19 Jun 2025, "Asal-usul Nama Candi Prambanan dan Dua Versi Cerita Pembangunannya"
note: [read via: secondary only; primary NOT opened] [tier B] Soekarto: Wanua Pangramwan (paṅramvan, home of Dhanada in the Poh charter) is "diduga" the origin of the name Prambanan (+ -an), supported by Cepit, Taji, Ijo, Kelurak. Area-level only (Prambanan spans Kab. Klaten and Kab. Sleman). Primary publication of the Soekarto claim not identified or opened. The systematic source is probably Kusen 1990/1991, "Identifikasi Toponim dalam Prasasti Jawa Kuno Abad IX-X dari Prambanan dan Sekitarnya dengan Toponim Masa Kini" (UGM research report; cited in the Indonesian Wikipedia article Prasasti Tulang Air I), NOT accessible.

name: paṇḍamuan
source_citation: Soekarto (initials and year not given by the relaying source), as relayed by Ahmad Yasin, Kompas.com 19 Jun 2025, "Asal-usul Nama Candi Prambanan dan Dua Versi Cerita Pembangunannya" ; plus Damais 1970:367-368 (cited in the DHARMA MantyasihIII commentary: paṅramuan is a phonetically later variant of paṇḍamuan)
note: [read via: DHARMA XML; Kompas relay; Damais NOT opened] [tier B] Chain of two published steps: (1) Damais: paṇḍamuan ~ paṅramuan/paṅramvan (variant); (2) Soekarto: Pangramwan ~ Prambanan. The chain is mine to state: neither author equates paṇḍamuan with Prambanan in the sources opened. Area-level only; paṇḍamuan occurs in 9 inscriptions and may not be one place.

name: rukam
modern_place: Between the kecamatan of Bulu and Kedu, Temanggung ("or slightly SE of it"), i.e. between wanua i wunut and wanua i kdu
source_citation: Muchtar, Agni Sesaria 2014, "Wanua I Rukam, Nama Asli Situs Liangan? (Kajian terhadap Prasasti Rukam 907 M ...)", in Liangan: Mozaik Peradaban Mataram Kuno di Lereng Sindoro (2014); as relayed (with quotation) by Ariyanto Mahardika, Tirto.id 21 Nov 2024
note: [read via: secondary only; Muchtar 2014 NOT opened] [tier B] Muchtar rejects the idea that Rukam is the village destroyed by the eruption and places Rukam near the watak patapan, "[antara wanua i wunut dengan wanua i kdu], atau sedikit agak ke tenggara", comparing Mantyasih I/III, Tulang Air I/II and Gondosuli II. Area-level, no desa. Wunut = Dusun Wunut, Desa Wonotirto, Kec. Bulu and Kdu = Desa Kedu, Kec. Kedu per Resiyani 2010 (via the same article). Rukam is a case where the identification literature is entangled with an archaeological site (Liyangan is discussed as the destroyed village, a different question); for T7 this is a circularity risk - do not use Rukam for matching without a domain expert.

name: rukam
source_citation: Budaya Indonesia (Kemendikbud portal), entry "Prasasti Rukam": "Diduga, Wanua i Rukam memang berada di sekitar wilayah Kabupaten Temanggung sekarang"; no scholar named. Competing view in the same entry: the village in the charter is "bukan Wanua i Rukam, melainkan desa yang belum diketahui namanya". Nastiti 1982 (Tiga Prasasti dari Masa Balitung) and Wisseman Christie (Register) read Rukam as a replacement for a vanished village.
note: [read via: portal; Nastiti/Christie NOT opened] [tier C/B] Region-level only. The charter was found at Desa Petarongan, Kec. Parakan (Temanggung) - a findspot, not an identification. A journalist (Tirto) also notes Dusun Tegalrukem (Ngrukem), Desa Campuranom, Kec. Bansari as a similar-sounding name, adding "belum ada penelitian untuk menautkan keduanya" - NOT recorded as I1 (name similarity, no scholar; belongs to I2).

name: tlaṁ
source_citation: Stutterheim 1934:282-283 (cited in the DHARMA TelangII-WanagiriII commentary)
note: [read via: DHARMA commentary; Stutterheim NOT opened] [tier A] Stutterheim identified tlaṁ as Teleng village in kec. Manyaran, "based on the assumption that the river mentioned in the text is the Solo River". Outside the primary frame (Wonogiri, not Kedu/Prambanan). Disputed by Nastiti 2015 (next row).

name: tlaṁ
source_citation: Nastiti, Titi Surti 2015:33-34 (cited in the DHARMA TelangII-WanagiriII commentary: "the most likely identifications were")
note: [read via: DHARMA commentary; Nastiti 2015 NOT opened] [tier A] Nastiti doubts Stutterheim because his two identifications are too far apart to form one sima; she proposes Teleng hamlet (Desa Sendang, Kec. Giriworyo) for tlaṁ and Jatiroto hamlet (Desa Wonoboyo, Kec. Wonogiri) for paparahuan (not in the frame). Two published identifications disagree - both recorded.

name: saliṅsiṅan
modern_place: West slope of Mt Merapi (Candi Asu or Candi Lumbung)
source_citation: Soekmono (no year in the commentary), on the basis of the findspot of the Sri Manggala stone; cited in the DHARMA Tihang commentary
note: [read via: DHARMA commentary; Soekmono NOT opened] [tier A] "Soekmono ... proposed that Salingsingan might be located on the west slope of Mount Merapi ... the dharma I saliṅsingan may refer to either Candi Asu or Candi Lumbung." The referent is the religious foundation (dharma) at Salingsingan, which may not be the village "Saliṅsiṅan, east of Parhyaṅan" of Sindoro-PuMamruk (the frame occurrence). No desa. Outside the primary frame.

name: saliṅsiṅan
modern_place: Rogoselo area (near Mt Goromanik, south of Pekalongan)
source_citation: Hadi Sidomulyo (no year in the commentary; comment on toponyms of the Tantu Panggelaran, entry Arega Sela), cited in the DHARMA Tihang commentary
note: [read via: DHARMA commentary; Sidomulyo NOT opened] [tier A] Sidomulyo concludes Salingsingan "may locate close to" Rogoselo (stele of Indrokilo found near Reban; a Muslim grave of "Pangeran Slingsingan" at Rogoselo). Conflicts with Soekmono (previous row). Far outside the Kedu/Prambanan frame. Same referent caveat as above.
